actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: SceneManipulation-v1 is registered with max_episode_steps=200
The environment supports the panda and fetch robots and creates a fetch agent by default
The environment is for explorations and visualization and has no success/failure metrics or rewards
evaluate() returns an empty dict, compute_dense_reward() returns 0, and the normalized dense reward divides that 0 by 1
reset accepts seed and options, including reconfigure and build or init config indices
The default scene builder is ReplicaCAD
The first supported observation mode is state
A None obs_mode selects the first supported observation mode, state
A state observation is the dict {agent, extra}; get_obs flattens it to one tensor
The agent's proprioception is its qpos and qvel, plus controller state only when the controller returns one
Fetch has 7 arm, 2 gripper, 3 body and 3 base joints
A None control_mode selects the first supported control mode, the first controller config key
The first Fetch controller config key is pd_joint_delta_pos with arm, gripper, body and base controllers
The Fetch arm delta controller is configured with raw joint bounds -0.1 to 0.1 for the 7 arm joints
The Fetch gripper is a mimic controller with one mimic entry mapping r_gripper_finger_joint to l_gripper_finger_joint and raw bounds -0.01 to 0.05
A mimic controller deduplicates its control joints and reads the joint limits at those indices, so this gripper has one action dimension
The Fetch body delta controller is configured with raw joint bounds -0.1 to 0.1 for the 3 body joints
The Fetch base forward velocity controller is configured with lower [-1, -3.14] and upper [1, 3.14]
The base forward velocity controller broadcasts its configured bounds to two action elements, forward velocity and rotation velocity
The joint position controller config defaults normalize_action to True
The joint velocity controller config defaults normalize_action to True
When a controller config enables normalize_action, ActuatorController.__init__ calls _clip_and_scale_action_space
_clip_and_scale_action_space replaces the configured Box with normalize_action_space(...) and keeps the raw low and high bounds for clipping and scaling
normalize_action_space returns Box(-1, 1) with the original shape
The combined controller flattens the named Box spaces into one Box with per-element low and high bounds
The simulation runs at 100 Hz and the control loop at 20 Hz, so every control step contains five simulation steps
A seeded reset sets the main RNG and the episode RNG to the seed; an unseeded reset samples the episode seed from the main RNG
step returns (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info); without success or fail in info, terminated is a zero tensor
A floating-point observation is converted to a Box with bounds -inf to inf
The observation space is the single observation space batched over num_envs

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the episode RNG, and one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; this package's fake draws its initial joint offsets with Python's random.Random, upstream uses numpy random states, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: rigid-body PhysX dynamics of a Fetch robot in a ReplicaCAD scene: contacts, friction, actuator forces, sensors and noise are the engine's, not this package's; no rendering or camera observation is served by the fake
the deployed model is the default fetch configuration with the pd_joint_delta_pos controller; other robots (panda) and other control modes have different action spaces and are not served here
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by timestep_ms (50 ms = five 20 Hz control steps) only

the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in, not a physics engine: it applies the 13 action values to the first 13 qpos entries and reports qvel from the last action, with no contacts, controller dynamics or asset loading; it was never compared with the upstream environment

the fake returns the unbatched 30-value state observation (15 qpos + 15 qvel); the upstream observation_space batches it to (1, 30) and the fake does not expose get_state/set_state, so no snapshot is offered on the fake (the upstream BaseEnv does define get_state/set_state)
no physical device is modelled and the model was never validated against one

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: no step or reset advances the simulated world after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the runtime latch; the last observation stays readable
